Subject: Procurement questionnaire — SLO definitions, telemetry access

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo last week — the technical team was impressed. Procurement at Acme needs a bit more color on how Redwood measures and exposes service guarantees before we can move forward. We're consolidating answers into a short questionnaire for Legal and our SREs. High-level asks: 

- Exact definitions for any availability/uptime SLOs you publish (calculation, error budget, measurement window).
- Latency SLOs: which percentile(s) you guarantee for generation endpoints and how you account for cold-starts/KV-cache effects.
- Monitoring & alerts: what monitoring sources (synthetic probes, infra metrics) contribute to SLO calculation, and what alert thresholds trigger customer-facing notifications.
- Customer access: can Acme have a read-only dashboard, a streaming export of SLO metrics, or scheduled CSV/JSON exports? Any limitations or sampling applied?
- Evidence: sample exports or proof points for the past 90 days (uptime summary, P95/P99 latency histograms).

Procurement timeline here is tight — we need responses by end of next week to keep our renewal timeline. I attached the procurement questionnaire worksheet (Acme_questionnaire.xlsx). Please confirm what you can provide and whether we need to sign an NDA for telemetry access.

Best,
Lara

Acme Software

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire — SLO definitions, telemetry access

Hi Lara — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together concise answers below and attached a short evidence packet. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call if you want to walk through any item.

1) Availability / uptime SLOs
- Public commitment: 99.95% availability per calendar month for Redwood-hosted inference endpoints (standard tier).
- Calculation: percentage of successful request completions (HTTP 2xx) divided by total requests, measured using both customer-facing production traffic telemetry and synthetic probes; outage windows are recorded in minutes. Error budget = 100% - SLO.
- Measurement window: rolling 30-day and calendar-month windows are maintained; contractual measurement for SLA credits uses calendar month.

2) Latency SLOs
- Typical guarantees: P95 latency target of 300ms and P99 latency target of 800ms for text-generation on our standard (non-quantized) model configurations under normal load.
- Accounting for cold-starts/KV cache: latency percentiles are computed on request-attempts that reach a warm serving instance; cold-starts are tracked separately and not included in the baseline SLO for steady-state endpoints. When customers use dedicated pools with pinned models we include warm-start metrics only. We document warm vs cold samples in the exported histogram metadata.

3) Data sources for monitoring & alerts
- SLOs are computed from a combination of: 1) production request telemetry (success/failure, response time), 2) synthetic health probes from regional vantage points, and 3) infra-level metrics (GPU health, queue lengths) for internal incident triage.
- Alerts: production SREs get P99 or availability drops via PagerDuty; customers receive notifications for sustained SLO degradation > 30 minutes and for incidents that meet the SLA incident definition. Thresholds are configurable for Dedicated customers as part of the onboarding doc.

4) Customer access to metrics
- Read-only Grafana dashboard: yes — we can invite Acme users to a tenant-isolated, read-only Grafana view with SLO panels, latency histograms, and recent incident logs.
- Scheduled exports: weekly CSV export of SLO aggregates (availability %, P50/P95/P99, error counts) can be delivered to an S3 bucket you control or emailed to a list.
- Sampling / limits: for very high-volume customers we apply streaming sampling to raw traces for storage efficiency; the aggregated percentiles we provide are computed on full request telemetry (no sampling for the percentiles).
- NDA: not required for read-only dashboards and exports under standard terms, but a Data Processing Addendum (DPA) and any corporate data sharing agreements are standard for Private deployments.

5) Evidence packet
- Attached: slo-evidence-summary.pdf (contains 90-day uptime summary, histogram snippets, and a short explanation of measurement methodology).
- Access: I can provision a read-only Grafana invite (dashboard-invite.ics) for two Acme users for a 30-day window while procurement completes review.

Next steps: tell me which Acme users you want invited and whether you prefer the weekly CSV export or a Grafana invite for the 30-day window. We'll also include Marissa (reliability) and Karthik (SRE infra) on any call.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Lara — quick follow-up with the specifics you asked for and next steps.

- Request size assumptions: the attached evidence uses a mixed request profile; for the P99 numbers referenced in the summary we filtered to requests with an average output of 512–768 tokens. For long-form (avg ~600 tokens) you should expect P95/P99 approximately in line with our stated targets, though dedicated pools improve tail latency. We will generate a short model-run tailored histogram for Acme's payload sample if you share a small representative prompt set.

- Cold-start rate: over the last 90 days cold-starts (instances starting from zero warm state) occurred on ~0.4% of requests across our multi-tenant hosted clusters; for dedicated pools the rate is <0.1%. We'll include a CSV with warm vs cold tags in the weekly export if you take the scheduled CSV option.

- SOC 2: Redwood maintains a SOC 2 Type II attestation. I'm linking the public download and attaching the relevant coversheet to the HubSpot record. Legal can use the SOC 2 report to validate controls around telemetry access; if they need an executed NDA or additional documentation we can coordinate with our security/compliance team.
